entry.title: MVW2012 Theorem 1 (p.2)
entry.subtitle: wiesner_ideal · A. Molina, T. Vidick, J. Watrous. Optimal counterfeiting attacks and generalizations for Wiesner's quantum money. TQC 2012, LNCS 7582, 45-64. arXiv:1202.4010v1

fields.label: Source and theorem
fields.text: MVW2012 Theorem 1 (p.2): optimal simple counterfeiting attack on Wiesner's scheme succeeds with probability exactly (3/4)^n.

fields.label: Assumptions
items: Bank note = n qubits, each uniformly and independently one of |0>,|1>,|+>,|-> (secret to the adversary).
Adversary receives exactly ONE valid note and applies any quantum channel to output two notes (simple counterfeiting).
No access to a verification oracle; no repeated or adaptive verification; no leaked post-measurement states (MVW2012 p.2 explicitly excludes these).
Bank verifies each candidate independently with the exact projective test (all n qubits must be correct; zero error tolerance, no loss).

fields.label: Parameters
fields.text: n: number of qubits per note, integer >= 1

fields.label: Quantifier over adversaries
fields.text: sup over ALL quantum channels (CPTP maps, unbounded ancilla and computation) from one note to two notes

fields.label: Numerical method
fields.text: log-space: log10 P = n*log10(3/4); float64 then cross-checked in Decimal(60 digits)

fields.label: Independent crosscheck
fields.text: qmint/proofs/checker.py (Decimal re-derivation); n=1 SDP value 3/4 is lane C (qmint/attacks) deliverable

fields.label: Caveats
items: Not a bound for noisy/threshold verifiers (that is game W2), lossy channels, oracle access, or S-money.
Does not cover the classical-verification variant (P-W1CV) and must not be used for it.

related.summary: Theorem 1. The optimal simple counterfeiting attack against Wiesner's quantum money scheme has success probability exactly (3/4)^n, where n is the number of qubits in each bank note.
